Carry-forward RESOLVED: the app-token vs personal-token rate-limit distinction is now spelled out in both files and in references/graphql-patterns.md. Personal tokens get 10M points/minute shared across reads and writes; app tokens get 5M per minute for reads and 5M for writes separately, so migrating an integration from a personal token to an app token halves its read ceiling.

Carry-forward RE-LOGGED: the binary is_israeli_holiday function still cannot express erev-chag half-days (Purim eve, seder day, Tisha B'Av). This cycle only added an in-code docstring saying so. A real fix needs a third state (half-day) and a caller contract for it, which is a bigger change than this cycle's budget allowed. Still deliberately listed as out of scope in references/domain-checklist.md.

Two inverted claims from the 1.4.0 cycle were corrected, both on the happy path. (1) The skill asserted multi-level boards are included by default in the `boards` query; the docs say the opposite, only `classic` boards return unless `hierarchy_type` or explicit IDs are passed. (2) Step 1's verify function read `account { plan { max_users } }`, and `account.plan` is documented to return null on multi-product-infrastructure accounts, so the very first step failed on exactly the newer accounts the skill will meet. Lesson: a claim inherited from a prior cycle's summary is not evidence; re-fetch the reference page for anything on the primary path.

Version drift was worse than a one-quarter slip: the skill pinned 2026-04, which entered maintenance on 2026-07-01 and is scheduled for deprecation in July 2027. Default is now 2026-07 and the RC is 2026-10, which also falsifies the 1.4.0 lesson that claimed no 2026-10 RC existed. Every code sample now pins 2026-07 explicitly rather than relying on the default.

Corrected a plan-model claim that was wrong in shape, not just in numbers: monday is four products with separate ladders, CRM tops out at Ultimate rather than Enterprise, Free exists only on work management, and paid plans start at a 3-seat minimum.

Found a claim inversion in the task brief itself: API access is NOT free on all plans. The pricing page caps daily API calls by tier (1,000/day Standard, 10,000 Pro, 25,000 Enterprise). On Standard this binds far earlier than the 10M complexity budget and makes a once-a-minute poll (1,440 calls/day) impossible by construction. Written up as the concrete reason to prefer webhooks.
